segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the verified drawing language, proportions, materials, surface wear and original colors of Picture 1 and Picture 2. Keep the adventurer's broad heavy adult body, short dark hair, thick beard, tired experienced face, dark teal-black layered worn cloak, purple cloth panels, red scarf and crossing straps, pale metal shoulder and chest structure, complete backpack and rolled load, heavy gloves and boots, and one cyan-lit waist lantern. Preserve the three-color foreground-middle-background hierarchy of the forest-lake scene. Reference fidelity overrides generic style wording.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use restrained readable 2D motion, compatible variable-weight linework, thin shading only where consistent with the references, soft diffuse light and clear separation of the three spatial layers. Let body weight, equipment width and a deliberate stop express the decision; avoid dramatic posing or montage.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show exactly one physical instance of the established adult adventurer. Picture 1 identity views all describe this one person. Keep the complete equipment system attached and connected. Because the reference is a full-body identity sheet, use only low-amplitude actions and stable body proportions.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): preserve the identity, existing elements, spatial continuity and original three-color hierarchy of SCENE-03. Use an existing visually supported narrowing between the foreground and middle-ground travel space only if Picture 2 actually provides it. Do not invent a gate, wall, bridge, rocks, roots, signs, rails, buildings or new path.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: begin with a slightly elevated medium-wide three-quarter view. Keep the adventurer's complete loaded silhouette, the visually supported direct route and an existing open side band readable within the foreground, middle ground and background. Preserve one screen direction. Hold the camera nearly fixed, allowing only a very slow approach push before he stops if the scene geometry supports it.

ACTION: the adventurer advances two slow heavy steps along the direct existing route. Before the complete backpack and rolled load enter the supported narrowing, he tests the available width by turning one shoulder a few degrees and placing one boot half a step forward. The full load remains attached. He recognizes that forcing the direct line would catch or compress the equipment, stops before contact and returns the testing boot to a stable stance. His eyes move toward the existing open side band while his torso stays grounded. End with both feet planted, one gloved hand resting lightly on an existing strap, and the complete load unchanged.

AUDIO DESIGN: quiet forest-lake air, distant water, restrained leaves, two heavy steps, cloth layers, strap tension, backpack weight and one boot settling back. A sparse non-melodic low tone narrows during the width test, cuts to near silence at the stop and remains unresolved as his gaze shifts. Audio supports weight, spatial judgment and restraint; it does not create MV rhythm.

NEGATIVE: no second character, duplicate adventurer, clone, split screen, four-person identity sheet, reflection person or shadow double; no removed backpack, dropped bedroll, discarded gear, new buckle, new tool, new weapon or duplicate lantern; no invented gate, wall, bridge, rocks, roots, sign, rail, building or path; no collision, scraping, squeeze-through, leap, run, acrobatics, panic, speed ramp, montage or music-video cutting; no young slim swordsman redesign, horns, tail, wings, clean modern armor or cyan-white energy body; no axis flip, reverse space, text, subtitle, logo, watermark, glossy 3D render or hard synthetic digital edges.

segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds, continuing directly from the selected real ending frame of Segment A.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the exact same Picture 1 adventurer, equipment connections, body mass, worn materials and original colors, and preserve the same Picture 2 forest-lake identity and three-color spatial hierarchy. The backpack, rolled load, cloak, scarf, straps, metal structure, gloves, boots and single waist lantern remain complete and unchanged.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use restrained readable low-amplitude movement, compatible line weight, reference-consistent shading, soft diffuse light and clear foreground-middle-background separation. Character charm comes from practical rerouting with the full burden, not from removing the burden or becoming suddenly agile.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show the same one physical adult adventurer from Segment A. Preserve the chosen real A ending pose and every existing equipment connection. Do not simplify, discard, duplicate or redesign the load.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): remain in the same verified SCENE-03 space, with the same direct narrowing, open side band, screen direction, lighting direction and three-color palette logic, but only where these relations are visually supported by Picture 2. Do not create new terrain or reveal an invented reverse area.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: inherit the same camera side and established spatial axis from Segment A. Use a medium-wide view that keeps his complete load and the verified open side band visible. Allow one restrained lateral follow through the existing open area if supported; otherwise keep the camera fixed. Preserve foreground, middle-ground and background continuity.

ACTION: from the held Segment A ending, the adventurer takes one complete step backward to recover turning space. He rotates his torso and full backpack together by a small controlled angle, keeping the rolled load and lantern attached. He then takes two slow diagonal steps through the existing open side band, following a shallow curved route around the supported narrowing. The equipment sways with believable weight but clears without contact. Once beyond the restricted line, he returns his shoulders toward the original travel direction and continues one measured step. End with the complete adventurer and all gear intact, having changed the route rather than forced the load through.

AUDIO DESIGN: continue the same forest-lake ambience and distant water, adding one heavy backward step, restrained cloth and strap friction, backpack weight shifting, two diagonal footfalls and a final settling step. The near-silence inherited from Segment A opens into a quiet low non-melodic release when the load clears the narrowing. Audio reinforces effort, geometry and calm judgment; it is not a song cue or MV beat track.

NEGATIVE: no second character, duplicate adventurer, clone, split screen, four-person identity sheet, reflection person or shadow double; no removed backpack, dropped bedroll, discarded gear, new buckle, tool, weapon or duplicate lantern; no invented gate, wall, bridge, rocks, roots, sign, rail, building, path or reverse terrain; no collision, squeeze-through, teleportation, leap, run, acrobatics, sudden nimble movement, triumph pose, speed ramp, montage or music-video cutting; no young slim redesign, horns, tail, wings, clean modern armor or cyan-white energy body; no axis flip, unrelated location, text, subtitle, logo, watermark, glossy 3D render or hard synthetic digital edges.
